issues.failure_explanation: Property itm:Udal relates a primal shifted term and a dual nonlinear difference only when the shift is the magnitude of one of the two arguments of A. In eq:Proofaaq34 the nonlinear difference is between the two traces of ∇e_h, but the shift is |∇v_h(T_+)|, which is unrelated because e_h=v_h-u_h. For example, for φ(t)=t^p/p with p>2, taking this shift large while both traces of ∇e_h remain bounded makes the primal side scale like a^{p-2}, whereas the dual expression scales like a^{2-p}; no shift-independent equivalence follows. Thus Case 2 does not prove the companion estimate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a new jump argument must control the nonlinear normal-jump case with the actual shift |∇v_h|, or the companion estimate and all later uses must be weakened accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The global companion estimate eq:Enrichment2 is unsupported. It is used to absorb companion errors in the main medius argument and to construct the conforming interpolation estimate, so both the nonconforming and conforming theorem chains become unreliable.
issues.title: Nonlinear jump equivalence is applied with an unrelated shift
issues.why_classification: The failed step is the central nonlinear companion estimate used by both principal proof chains, and the source supplies no valid replacement compatible with the required shift. Repair requires new proof architecture rather than local algebra.

issues.failure_explanation: On each element, Π_0 averages ∇u-χ_\tria, but the function applied to that average is φ_{|∇u(x)|}, whose shift varies with x. Ordinary Jensen's inequality applies to one fixed convex function and therefore does not justify integrating φ_{|∇u(x)|}(|Π_0(∇u-χ_\tria)|) against the same variable shifts. Establishing such a bound would require a nontrivial shifted-average stability argument that is absent.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a valid local stability lemma for averaging in shifted modulars, including the necessary shift-change estimates, or replace the stated best-approximation bounds by a quantity directly controlling the interpolation error.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed reduction of the CR interpolation error to the best piecewise-constant approximation of F(∇u) is unproved. The same estimate is subsequently reused in the conforming interpolation and conforming FEM arguments.
issues.title: Jensen's inequality is used for an elementwise varying shifted integrand
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial new averaging lemma could plausibly preserve the advertised rates and theorem forms; the defect is more than routine algebra but does not by itself force a new global proof strategy.

issues.failure_explanation: The companion lemma yields a divergence contribution in the conjugate shifted modular (φ_{|∇v|})^*, but the theorem and its proof state the primal modular φ_{|∇v|}. These are not uniformly interchangeable for general N-functions; for φ(t)=t^p/p with p≠2 they have different growth exponents. The later appeal to the oscillation lemma also controls only the conjugate modular.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the divergence contribution throughout the approximation theorem and its proof by the conjugate shifted modular, and consistently use that corrected term in the proof of thm:AprioriConf.
issues.overall_effect: The stated conforming interpolation estimate is not established, and the proof of the localized conforming FEM estimate cannot convert its displayed primal data term into the defined oscillation.
issues.title: The conforming approximation theorem replaces the required conjugate modular by the primal modular
issues.why_classification: The correction is localized and aligns the argument with the existing companion and oscillation lemmas, preserving the final conforming FEM claim, but it materially changes the auxiliary theorem's stated data norm.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\item we increase $\varepsilon_+$ by a factor of 2 if $\eta_+^2$ is the largest error indicator,
\item we decrease $\varepsilon_-$ by a factor 1/2 if $\eta_-^2$ is the largest error indicator,

issues.failure_explanation: The quantities η_- and η_+ are defined by evaluating regularized energies at u_h, the exact minimizer of the original discrete problem. That solution is precisely unavailable during the iterative computation. Consequently the algorithm cannot determine which relaxation indicator is largest and cannot execute its prescribed update rule from the stated inputs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, η_- and η_+ must be replaced by computable quantities or rigorously computable bounds based only on available iterates and data, with an update rule justified for those replacements.
issues.overall_effect: The adaptive scheme described for the experiments is not an executable procedure as written, so its claimed mechanism for choosing relaxation updates is unsupported.
issues.title: Adaptive relaxation indicators require the unknown exact discrete minimizer
issues.why_classification: The source gives no way to evaluate the indicators governing two branches of the algorithm. Making the scheme executable requires a new estimator or construction, not a local correction.
